column8: Tue 17 Nov: claim 2's audited base for 3.0 and 3a (Juming's 2022 gap of NT$25.06m, tickets 31.49%, government 3.31%); arithmetic checked; a store figure, at most one clause.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for claim 2: the running gap was there 12 years in (NT$20m a year raised outside, 2011); not like-for-like with row 1's 2022 total.
Tue 17 Nov: same point as Q100-001 (tickets do not pay Juming's running costs) in the museum's own appeal words; Q100-001's audited table is the stronger evidence.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; keep the museum's quotes, drop the NT$2m and NT$177m property figures until read on the court's record (secondary aggregator), and note registered property includes land and works, not cash.

Tue 17 Nov: a flood is a site shock, so in Laura's plan it meets her flexibility or co-sponsors (3b; 3e: the plan secures the money, not the site), never the operating reserve; drop the 3a use; carry Q101-043's 136 damaged works here.

Tue 17 Nov: possible 3.0 clause: Taiwan's best-known artist-founder named keeping it going among the three hardest parts; quoted second-hand in a 2003 thesis; her ten are a base for running it, not its budget (H9-119).
Tue 17 Nov: store support for claim 3: even Chimei's running money is a yearly charter grant (NT$35m, 2024); Q100-036's December board vote makes the sharper 3d point.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; IPS l.9 in a founder's own books, but the museum still got its grant and the link to Chi Mei's loss is timing only; say can, never fall together (Q50).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3d guard: the one large Taiwan fund is permanent and spends income, while Laura's reserve is spent down one dated payment at a time; arithmetic checked (19.6 and 2.3 years); never call her reserve an endowment.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a contrast: a NT$660m fund's interest could not run a museum, while each of Laura's payments rests on an instrument that pays on its date; cite as a 2003 museum head, since the speaker is inferred.
Tue 17 Nov: store note for 3d (company giving can track profit); say the 10% cap as the 2003 rule, never in the present tense, since today's Income Tax Act limit is unchecked.
Tue 17 Nov: store evidence for Q100-041 (the company covered about a third, the chairman the rest each year); not artist-founded; attribution by page order.
Tue 17 Nov: store evidence for 3a or 2.3 beside IPS l.9: a director named the parent-company risk about a year before the museum lost its space (Q11d-024 holds the loss); attribution by page order.
Tue 17 Nov: store evidence for Q100-041: a museum whose running money was its founder's business closed with that business six years in; a builder's museum, not an artist's.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d guard with a Taiwan reason: officials gave less to museums they thought rich, so never pitch her ten owned years as a reason the state need not help, nor as an anchor or match.
Tue 17 Nov: store evidence for Q100-041 (closed in 1985 with the founder's finances, after a scandal); KNOWN in Taiwan, rare for a Wharton judge.
Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 or 3a contrast in a founder's own words: he had to earn NT$14m each year to run it, while Laura's ten are owned before 2033; NT$1.64m is context, never her residency's cost.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for claim 1: outside money came a decade or two on and for named projects; close to the pattern of Q11e-035.
Tue 17 Nov: 3.0's clearest Taiwan statement of the model: a family must earn NT$25m of profit a year to carry the running costs; a collector's museum, not an artist's.

Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 store note; the 4.3 times sets $500,000 of face against the $115,000 top, so say face dollars or use $399,089 (NUMBERS 8h), about 3.5 times; the building remark is context, never a cost.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; one rural quote doubling adds little to Q5d's base rates for Table 3 row 7; never an estimate for Laura's building.
Tue 17 Nov: store evidence for claims 1-3 (an artist's family built with a loan and runs on almost nothing; succession named as a hard problem).
Tue 17 Nov: store evidence that family galleries survive on persistence without money set aside; a student report, not peer-reviewed.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d support for the founder pays first: the biggest co-sponsor gift found came 35 years on, for visible persistence; one donor's reasons and a capital gift; never about the founder's share.
Tue 17 Nov: store contrast: the artist's works were the reserve, sold when needed; pairs with Q101-002; never imply shares are sold to pay a payment (IPS l.11).
Tue 17 Nov: store nuance for Q100-041: the usual answer to a running gap was opening less (half-closing, appointments) or selling works, not closing.
Tue 17 Nov: store base rate from two theses that tickets do not pay running costs; the 2007 thesis read as an abstract only.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d note, but from one New Taipei museum forum; say it of private museums, never of residencies, where the Ministry's village grants pay yearly running costs (Q10d-009).
Tue 17 Nov: same case as Q100-030 (IT Park run on the founder's photography surplus); carry the NT$170,000 a month (2001) as context only.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3.0's one Taiwan example of IPS l.9: a career paid for an artist-run space for 37 years and its end ended the space; say rest, not closure, and leave the blog's borrowing detail out.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for 3d and 3e area (3): co-sponsors paid in short fixed terms, three years at most; beside Q50-008 and Q55-001.
Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 note; say owned years free some of that time, since her ten are a base and the residency still raises the rest (H9-119); two practitioners' views.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; key-person risk, and the building lived on under a new operator; whether payments continue without Laura is outside the case.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; drop the analogy: Laura plans to establish the residency (case l.76), so she is not an outside contributor to an institution others run.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d half-clause support, but registered funds are legal minimums that include land and works, Juming's is secondary and its 2026 figure exceeds a year; say no case found showed a year of running costs set aside at opening, never none of the 13.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d contrast: Chi Mei, the best-known corporate museum backer, still votes its donation each December, while Laura's ten need no vote; read in Chi Mei's own filings.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q11d-023 (Chimei's tickets cover about half, the company the rest); carry the 2003 free-entry figures there.
Tue 17 Nov: store horizon note: her commitment needs ten dated years, not permanence (the case puts after 2042 out of scope); never the 40-50 year figure, which is unsourced.
Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 context only; drop residency-sized, which reads as costing the residency; say her NT$1.64m is below every case's yearly running cost, so a base, not a budget; mixed years.

Tue 17 Nov: 3b evidence beside Q11e-033, but only Juming is among the praised founders; say founder-funded places with nothing set aside met shocks by appeal, sale or borrowing, and her half meets IPS l.15's three uses, never giving less.

Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 and 3a, IPS l.9 in Taiwan's own record; say most of each payment is owned January 2027 and the rest January 2028, never all from 2027; cases found, not a census; test cold first, since the Taiwan halls row failed by inviting what after 2042.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a outside yardstick from the artists' own adviser: fund the first years without art sales; Laura's ten do it for ten years in Treasuries; say advice for artists' foundations, not a standard, and initially means the first years.
Tue 17 Nov: pairs with Q101-001 for 3a: without money set aside at the start, study centres sell their works to run; never call Laura's reserve an endowment.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for IPS l.9: art alone funds a foundation only if it sells; Laura's payments do not rest on her career's market.
Tue 17 Nov: same idea as Q101-003 (assuming art alone will fund a foundation); about estate-distribution foundations.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for claim 1 and 3b: house museums strain against estate plans and turn to public money; the case already plans co-sponsors for the facility.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a US accreditation rule on sale proceeds serves no part.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 contrast if room (70% of the field's assets in art, 2015); drop the unsourced superlative most concentrated portfolios in philanthropy; Laura's residency is not an artist-endowed foundation.
Tue 17 Nov: store correction to claim 2: by count 46% held only financial assets in 2005; most hold art is true of the dollars, not the foundations.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for Q101-007: programme-running foundations were the most art-heavy (74%, 2005).
Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 contrast: living founders' foundations run pass-through, spending each year's gift, while Laura owns ten years before the first payment; Jentel (Q32-031) is the case.
Tue 17 Nov: 3.0 store note (main money arrives about 18 years on, at death); the cited study was not read; never as no other founder can, which SKELETON 3.0 cut as untestable.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for IPS l.9 (founders' gifts fell from 66.5% to 26.7% of revenue, 1995-2000); the study says cause cannot be confirmed; cite IPS l.9, partly true per CANON B4.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for 2.3: art can fall in the same downturn as shares; say a downturn that can cut co-sponsors, never one that cuts them (Q50).
Tue 17 Nov: possible conceit or 3e note: a value that did not move in 2008 was unpriced, not safe; the study only speculates on the cause.
Tue 17 Nov: store contrast: forced block sales are discounted and borrowing against future sales is pencil; Laura's payments need neither.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; one sentence naming flexibility as the design question, loosely beside the half kept; not a finding.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a base rate beside Q9-016: 44% of ended foundations were spent out or never funded (Keel arithmetic); drop than buildings do, since the reasons list has no building category, and 28% ended as planned.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; operating foundations spend on operations, true but serves no part.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e site limit (the plan secures the money, not the site); never the first artist-founded residency, since Yaddo (1900) and MacDowell (1907) had artist co-founders; say an early one, 1918.
Tue 17 Nov: store context for Q101-021 (a residency run from an owned fortune, 3.4% of book assets spent in FY2025); arithmetic checked.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e limit beside Q9c's site closures: even an owned fortune did not keep a storm-hit site; said as a limit on the site, never as comfort for the payments.
Tue 17 Nov: same event as Q101-021 (Captiva from Hurricane Ian to sale); carry the storm-to-sale timeline; the price is unconfirmed.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a size marker with conflicting counts.
Tue 17 Nov: store case of money before the place (17 years to opening), but forced by an estate's settling, not chosen; Q9-009 carries the principle.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a founder's institution that takes no gifts needs a large owned base; 2014, and it later took a Mellon grant.
Tue 17 Nov: store contrast only; paying operations from art sales would clash with IPS l.11 if offered as a model.
Tue 17 Nov: store support for Q101-007 and 2.3 (one residency-running foundation 75.7% in the founder's art); arithmetic checked.
Tue 17 Nov: conceit candidate for 3.0 or 2.3: the same paintings at $22.8m book and $437.3m market on one form, pencil until sold; one turn, never in tables or Laura's words.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; art's carrying cost (0.16% a year, arithmetic checked) serves no part.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; drop the $50,000-as-2.5% and per-artist comparisons, which read as costing the residency, and fix the on-site count (16 with 2 virtual against 13 named).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; programme terms are the residency's business, which SKELETON 3d cuts.
Tue 17 Nov: store only beside Q32-031; drop $50,000 as seven or eight Jentel residencies, a per-artist costing in 2008 US money.
Tue 17 Nov: store contrast for 3.0: one painting bought a building and two years of running, then yearly grants; read through search excerpts.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the grant figure comes via an aggregator and covers all of Le Korsa's work.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; sales of assets mix securities and art; arithmetic checked.
Tue 17 Nov: store failure case for reserves before buildings: buildings, debt and little cash; heirs not named; search excerpts.
Tue 17 Nov: store or conceit note: art-rich and cash-poor (spending 0.40% of assets in 2005), a large pencil figure that pays no bills; arithmetic checked.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the lot count conflicts (26 against 25 of 36), so say about two dozen works with the source named.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; one historic restoration with conflicting final costs ($23m or $28m), never set against her flexibility (aha row 8's guard); Q5d holds the base rates.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; say public charity since FY2013, the year 101 Spring Street opened, as timing, not that the building pushed it.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; trustees chose to end rather than sell the core asset.
Tue 17 Nov: store parallel for 3b: one estate split the money from the building and gave the house to a university to run; transfer terms not read.
Tue 17 Nov: same event as Q100-005 (Juming after the October 2024 flood), which was read at source; carry the 136 damaged works there.
Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 contrast if room; the parallel is concentration, not unsellability, since the foundations can and do sell the art; a Keel inference, never the IPS's own claim.
